messages.subject: rmr2 environmental issue
parts:
Setup:

I have 2 identical servers running R version 3.1.0
rmr2 is 2.3.0
CDH 4.6

I run the following script: 

Sys.setenv(HADOOP_STREAMING="/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH/lib/hadoop-mapreduce/hadoop-streaming-2.0.0-cdh4.6.0.jar")
Sys.setenv(HADOOP_CMD="/usr/bin/hadoop")
library(rmr2)
library(rhdfs)
hdfs.init()
ints = to.dfs(1:100)
calc = mapreduce(input = ints, map = function(k, v) cbind(v, 2*v))

Problem:

One server runs fine, I get the results without issue. The other server launches the M/R job but I get the following output in the task logs:

java.lang.RuntimeException: java.lang.RuntimeException: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: Class org.apache.hadoop.streaming.AutoInputFormat not found
        at org.apache.hadoop.conf.Configuration.getClass(Configuration.java:1806)
        at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.JobConf.getInputFormat(JobConf.java:620)
        at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.MapTask.runOldMapper(MapTask.java:394)
        at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.MapTask.run(MapTask.java:332)
        at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.Child$4.run(Child.java:268)

Observation:
  1. on the "bad" server I see the following two messages I don't see on the "good" server after executing the line
ints = to.dfs(1:100)

DEPRECATED: Use of this script to execute hdfs command is deprecated.
Instead use the hdfs command for it.
Warning message:
In to.dfs(1:100) : Converting to.dfs argument to keyval with a NULL key 

****I don't think this has anything to do with it but I thought it was worth noting...

Verification Steps:
  1. Verified location of streaming jar and the class was actually in the jar file
  2. Verified Hadoop files are the same on both systems
  3. Verified rmr2/rhdfs packages are the same
  4. Verified environment variables are identical
  5. Verified the /etc/hadoop/conf files are identical too

Any other thoughts on what I can try? I can't re-install CDH here because there are other applications using it happily without issue and I don't want to disturb their configuration. 

Please let me know.

Thanks,
Brendan

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1592] rmr2 environmental issue
parts:
On Fri, Aug 8, 2014 at 8:12 AM, bayroot22 <bsc...@hotmail.com> wrote:
Setup:

I have 2 identical servers running R version 3.1.0
rmr2 is 2.3.0
CDH 4.6

I run the following script: 

Sys.setenv(HADOOP_STREAMING="/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH/lib/hadoop-mapreduce/hadoop-streaming-2.0.0-cdh4.6.0.jar")
Sys.setenv(HADOOP_CMD="/usr/bin/hadoop")
library(rmr2)
library(rhdfs)
hdfs.init()
ints = to.dfs(1:100)
calc = mapreduce(input = ints, map = function(k, v) cbind(v, 2*v))

Problem:

One server runs fine, I get the results without issue. The other server launches the M/R job but I get the following output in the task logs:

java.lang.RuntimeException: java.lang.RuntimeException: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: Class org.apache.hadoop.streaming.AutoInputFormat not found

This must be related to your CLASSPATH. This class is not distributed with R. R issues a command like

hadoop jar streaming.jar -inputformat org.apache.hadoop.streaming.AutoInputFormat ...

That class has to be available to hadoop. I would suggest running one of the hadoop streaming examples that come with hadoop with that option to see what happens, I am pretty sure this is a java problem independent of R. I hate it when support people tell me "not our problem" but we need to count on something and that's hadoop streaming working properly. I don't think it is here.

at org.apache.hadoop.conf.Configuration.getClass(Configuration.java:1806)
        at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.JobConf.getInputFormat(JobConf.java:620)
        at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.MapTask.runOldMapper(MapTask.java:394)
        at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.MapTask.run(MapTask.java:332)
        at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.Child$4.run(Child.java:268)

Observation:
  1. on the "bad" server I see the following two messages I don't see on the "good" server after executing the line
ints = to.dfs(1:100)

DEPRECATED: Use of this script to execute hdfs command is deprecated.
Instead use the hdfs command for it.
Warning message:
In to.dfs(1:100) : Converting to.dfs argument to keyval with a NULL key 

****I don't think this has anything to do with it but I thought it was worth noting...

What this is saying indirectly is that rmr can not find the hdfs program and therefore has to use hadoop dfs. This points to differences in how hadoop is installed on the two systems or the value of the PATH variable. So you are right it's not related, but it reveals the two systems are not installed identically. Trying to figure out why that difference occurs my help solving the main problem.


Antonio

  1. Verified location of streaming jar and the class was actually in the jar file

  3. Verified rmr2/rhdfs packages are the same
  4. Verified environment variables are identical
  5. Verified the /etc/hadoop/conf files are identical too

Any other thoughts on what I can try? I can't re-install CDH here because there are other applications using it happily without issue and I don't want to disturb their configuration. 

Please let me know.

Thanks,
Brendan
